criteria.suggestion: Asking earlier without context of camera usage doesn't feel trustworthy

criteria.title: Viewfinder and capture button
criteria.description: A full-screen viewfinder with a clearly positioned, large capture button
criteria.suggestion: Button should be reachable by thumb at the bottom of the screen

criteria.title: Flash controls
criteria.description: Flash toggle accessible without leaving the capture screen, with auto, on, and off states clearly indicated

criteria.title: Camera flip
criteria.description: A clear camera flip button accessible during capture, positioned so it is not accidentally triggered during shooting

criteria.title: Post-capture preview
criteria.description: A preview shown after capturing, giving the user the chance to retake or confirm before the media is used

criteria.title: Gallery picker of captures
criteria.description: The option to open photo library containing only photos captured within that series until exit of camera

checklists.name: Chat
checklists.description: The one-to-one or group messaging screen, handling keyboard behaviour, message input, media sharing, and real-time updates in the constraints of a mobile screen.

criteria.title: Keyboard push-up
criteria.description: The message input bar rising with the keyboard when it opens, so the conversation history is not obscured
criteria.suggestion: The behaviour differs between iOS and Android, so explicit handling on both platforms is what prevents the common bug of the keyboard obscuring the input bar

criteria.title: Input bar
criteria.description: A persistent input bar at the bottom of the screen containing a text field, send button, and media attachment option, thumb-reachable in all grip positions

criteria.title: Message bubbles
criteria.description: Sent messages on the right, received on the left, consistent with every messaging convention the user already knows
criteria.suggestion: Breaking the sent-right received-left convention for a design reason is rarely worth the disorientation it causes

criteria.title: Swipe to reply
criteria.description: Swiping a message right revealing a reply-to action, threading the response to the specific message

criteria.title: Long press message actions
criteria.description: Long pressing a message opening a reaction picker and action menu e.g. react, reply, copy, delete

criteria.title: Read receipts
criteria.description: Sent message status shown as subtle indicators below or within the message bubble (sent, delivered, read)

criteria.title: Media and file sharing
criteria.description: Images, videos, and files shareable directly from the input bar, with inline previews in the conversation thread

criteria.title: Typing indicator
criteria.description: An animated indicator when the other party is composing

criteria.title: Scroll to latest
criteria.description: When new messages arrive while the user is scrolled up, a button to jump to the latest message

checklists.name: Checkout
checklists.description: The payment flow on mobile optimised for native payment methods and the constraints of a small screen.

criteria.title: Native payment methods
criteria.description: Apple Pay and Google Pay as the primary checkout options, to complete the purchase with a single biometric tap.
criteria.suggestion: It is important to still offer manual card entry if you feel users will be concerned about 3rd part tool usage

criteria.title: Persistent order summary
criteria.description: The item list, quantities, and total available throughout the checkout flow — either persistently visible or accessible with a single tap

criteria.title: Minimal form fields
criteria.description: Only the fields genuinely required to complete the purchase e.g. card details, delivery address

criteria.title: Autofill capabilities
criteria.description: Shipping address fields that support iOS and Android autofill, removing the need to type a full address manually.

criteria.title: Keyboard types per field
criteria.description: Appropriate keyboard types throughout checkout e.g. numeric for card numbers and CVV, date or numeric pad for expiry.

criteria.title: Checkout progress
criteria.description: A clear step indicator for a multi-step experience e.g. having a Details, Payment and Checkout page separately

criteria.title: Error recovery
criteria.description: The experience after a payment failure, returning to the payment step with all previously entered data intact and a clear explanation of the reason

criteria.title: Order/payment confirmation
criteria.description: A clear confirmation screen with summary, payment method and amount, along with any other relevant information e.g. expected arrival date if it involves physical delivery
criteria.suggestion: It's common to email the user an invoice or payment confirmation, which the user can be reminded of here so they know they don't have to keep this page open in the app

checklists.name: Gesture navigation
checklists.description: The touch-based interaction patterns that let users navigate and act without tapping buttons.

criteria.title: Swipe to go back
criteria.description: The standard action to allow a user to go back without tapping a button
criteria.suggestion: This can be disabled on screens where a horizontal swipe exists to not be a conflict

criteria.title: List item swipe actions
criteria.description: Revealing quick actions such as delete, archive, mark as read on an item without opening it
criteria.suggestion: Suitable only if there are 2-3 actions available on the item, any more may be too significant space was

criteria.title: Pull to refresh
criteria.description: For scrollable content lists with a visible indicator and haptic confirmation when triggered

criteria.title: Long press menus
criteria.description: Triggered by long pressing, an item reveals actions relevant to that specific element
criteria.suggestion: These are utilised for quick actions, and the action should exist elsewhere in a more accessible way in the app

criteria.title: Pinch to zoom
criteria.description: Image and map content supporting standard pinch-to-zoom, with zoom level reset logically on navigation away

criteria.title: Drag to reorder
criteria.description: Lists or cards that can be reordered supporting long-press-to-lift and drag, with clear visual feedback during the drag state

criteria.title: Gesture hints
criteria.description: A subtle animation or tooltip on first encounter with a key gesture, hinting at its existence
criteria.suggestion: If it's a significant value to learn the gesture, the hint could persist until the user tries the action, so they understand it better

criteria.title: Haptic feedback
criteria.description: Beneficial for key gesture moments where your finger may cover the screen and therefore it's not clear whether you have engaged with the gesture e.g. the pull-to-refresh, long press or drag actions

checklists.name: In-App Browser
checklists.description: A browser experience inside a mobile app, which is handy for opening web links or accessing web data via API.

criteria.title: URL bar visibility
criteria.description: The URL of the current page visible to the user, confirming the domain before they interact with any forms or enter credentials
criteria.suggestion: Users who cannot see the URL in an in-app browser cannot verify they are on a legitimate domain, since URL visibility is a security baseline

criteria.title: Close action
criteria.description: A clear, persistent button for closing the browser and returning to the app (typically in a fixed toolbar rather than hidden behind a gesture)

criteria.title: Open in external default browser action
criteria.description: An option to open the URL in the user's default browser, while preserving the in-app browser experience still

criteria.title: Share action
criteria.description: Allowing the URL to be shared without opening the default browser

criteria.title: Loading feedback
criteria.description: A progress indicator while the page loads (either a top progress bar or an activity indicator) so the user knows the browser is working

checklists.name: In-App Notifications
checklists.description: The in-app feed of alerts, updates, and messages the user has received — distinct from system push notifications.

criteria.title: Reverse chronological order
criteria.description: Newest notifications at the top means users don’t have to scroll for the latest

criteria.title: Unread indicators
criteria.description: Unread notifications visually distinct from read ones e.g. a dot, bolder text, or a background colour difference

criteria.title: Mark all as read
criteria.description: A single action to clear all unread indicators at once
criteria.suggestion: Essential for an app with many notifications, or where there is likelihood the user spends a long time away

criteria.title: Notification grouping
criteria.description: Related notifications grouped together e.g. multiple comments on the same post shown as a single expandable item, not separate rows
criteria.suggestion: Best applied to high-activity content

criteria.title: Swipe to dismiss action
criteria.description: Individual notifications dismissible by swiping left, revealing a delete action

criteria.title: Deep link on tap
criteria.description: Tapping a notification navigates the user directly to the relevant content

criteria.title: Empty state
criteria.description: For when there are no notifications, to indicate they haven’t received any… yet

criteria.title: Settings shortcut
criteria.description: A direct link from the notifications screen to notification preferences, for users who want to adjust what they receive

criteria.title: Notification content
criteria.description: Information relevant to triggering the notification e.g. the change, author and time it occurred

checklists.name: Map View
checklists.description: The native map screen showing location-based content, user position, and contextual overlays

criteria.title: Pin and marker designs
criteria.description: Custom markers clearly distinguishable from each other and from the base map, sized for reliable tap accuracy on mobile
criteria.suggestion: Ensure the marker design for current location is the most prominent, as all map view interactions are centred around it

criteria.title: Marker clustering (if applicable)
criteria.description: How markers are shown when a group of them are so close together they cannot be shown individually, and must be grouped

criteria.title: Native map components
criteria.description: Leverage either MapKit for iOS or Google Maps for Android to utilise existing foundations and layout that is time consuming to create from scratch

criteria.title: Location permission
criteria.description: The point in the flow at which location permission is requested, with context explaining the level of access needed and why
criteria.suggestion: Consider the UI if permissions are denied, where you can provide instructions on how to change the permission in settings

criteria.title: Current location re-centre
criteria.description: A clearly visible button to re-centre the map to the user's current position without zooming or scrolling to it

criteria.title: Selected item bottom sheet
criteria.description: Tapping a marker expanding a bottom sheet with details about that location — not a full-screen navigation away from the map.

criteria.title: Search or filter actions
criteria.description: Search or filter controls accessible as a persistent overlay on the map or as a separate screen
criteria.suggestion: Selecting filters can be on a separate screen, but when on map the applied filters should be visible for context

criteria.title: Offline handling
criteria.description: When offline, cached map tiles displayed where available, with a clear indicator that the map may not be current

checklists.name: Onboarding
checklists.description: The first-run experience that orients a new user, collects necessary setup information, and delivers an early sense of the app value

criteria.title: Steps
criteria.description: The number of steps in the onboarding flow, limited to what is genuinely required before the app can be used
criteria.suggestion: Steps that can be deferred without preventing the app from functioning on day one consistently belong later, not in onboarding

criteria.title: Progress indicator
criteria.description: A clear indication of how many steps remain and where in the sequence the user currently is
criteria.suggestion: Users who can see the end of onboarding are significantly less likely to abandon it than those who feel they are in a tunnel

criteria.title: Step navigation
criteria.description: A clear mechanism for advancing through steps e.g. a 'next' button or a horizontal swipe gesture

criteria.title: Contextual permissions
criteria.description: Permissions surfaced at their contextually relevant moment within onboarding, rather than grouped at the start
criteria.suggestion: Grouping all permission requests at the beginning can lead to denials given lack of context

criteria.title: Skip option
criteria.description: A visible way to exit onboarding early and explore the app, with setup available to complete later
criteria.suggestion: Users who skip and explore freely often complete setup voluntarily once they understand the value

criteria.title: Personalisation step
criteria.description: One or two choices that make the app feel tailored from the start e.g. your name, interests, a key piece of information that applies to the product

criteria.title: Keyboard handling
criteria.description: Views that adjust correctly when the keyboard appears, appropriate keyboard types per field, and Next advancing to the following input

checklists.name: Onboarding Checklist
checklists.description: The in-app progress checklist that guides a new user through key setup steps to learn how the product works by completing actions.

criteria.title: Card or sheet presentation
criteria.description: The checklist presented as a dismissible bottom sheet or a persistent card on the home screen, not a full-screen overlay

criteria.title: Task count and progress
criteria.description: A visible count of completed versus total tasks and a progress bar or ring that updates as steps are completed

criteria.title: Tap to start each task
criteria.description: Each checklist item tappable, navigating directly to the relevant screen or feature not just informational

criteria.title: Completion celebration
criteria.description: When all tasks are complete, show a brief celebratory moment before the checklist disappears (animation, confetti, congratulatory message)

criteria.title: Dismissible action
criteria.description: The checklist is dismissible for users who do not want it not a forced guided path.
criteria.suggestion: Making the checklist dismissible is fair because sometimes users don't want or need guidance

criteria.title: Persistent but unobtrusive
criteria.description: The checklist is accessible from a consistent location (dashboard, profile, home)

criteria.title: Personalised to user type (if applicable)
criteria.description: If there are different user types or ways to use the app, include onboarding questions that direct to tailored steps in this checklist so it feels more personal

checklists.name: Paywall
checklists.description: A hard gate that blocks access to locked content and offers a path to subscribe.

criteria.title: Locked feature context and breakdown
criteria.description: A clear statement or short list of which specific feature/s the user is being blocked from accessing

criteria.title: Upgrade CTA
criteria.description: The primary action to start a subscription or free trial, positioned prominently on the paywall screen
criteria.suggestion: Be specific with what is unlocked e.g. "Unlock unlimited projects" or "Access full library"

criteria.title: Free trial offer
criteria.description: A clear statement of any trial period available before subscription billing begins.
criteria.suggestion: 'Try free for 7 days' framed as low-commitment is consistently one of the highest-converting messages on a paywall.

criteria.title: Dismiss action
criteria.description: A clear, neutral way to close the paywall and return to the free experience
criteria.suggestion: This should be obvious and accessible for the user to do

criteria.title: Restore purchases
criteria.description: A way for existing subscribers to recover their access after reinstalling or signing in on a new device

criteria.title: No guilt language
criteria.description: Dismiss and decline actions written in neutral language, without shaming or pressuring users into subscribing
criteria.suggestion: 'No thanks, I don't want to save money' is manipulative and unnecessary

checklists.name: Search
checklists.description: The search experience on mobile where keyboard handling and filtering results are unique to web.

criteria.title: Sticky search bar
criteria.description: The search input fixed at the top of the screen as results scroll beneath it
criteria.suggestion: A search bar that scrolls away with results forces users to scroll back up if they need to refine their query

criteria.title: Keyboard auto-focus
criteria.description: The keyboard opens immediately when the user navigates to the search screen — no extra tap required to start typing

criteria.title: Live results
criteria.description: Results updating as the user types rather than requiring a submit tap

criteria.title: Recent searches
criteria.description: Previously searched terms shown before the user starts typing for convenience to revisit results

criteria.title: Filter bottom sheet
criteria.description: Filtering accessed via a bottom sheet rather than a separate screen, to keep the search context visible while adjusting
criteria.suggestion: A full-screen filter page can be better if the filtering is extensive e.g. a retail store or booking system

criteria.title: Skeleton loading
criteria.description: Skeleton cards in the expected result shape shown while results load as user types

criteria.title: No results state
criteria.description: A helpful empty state with suggestions e.g. suggestion to check spelling, remove filters or try related terms

criteria.title: Clear query button
criteria.description: An action inside or near the search field to clear the current query with one tap

checklists.name: Settings
checklists.description: The screen where users manage their account, preferences, notifications, and app behaviour.

criteria.title: Grouped table layout
criteria.description: Settings organised into clearly labelled sections (Account, Notifications, Privacy, Support) using the native grouped list pattern
criteria.suggestion: Grouped settings are a platform convention users have deeply internalised. Deviating from it forces users to relearn navigation they already know

criteria.title: Native toggle controls
criteria.description: Binary settings presented with the platform-native toggle switch (UISwitch on iOS, Material Switch on Android)
criteria.suggestion: Custom toggles that look slightly off from the native ones create subtle distrust, since the difference is small but users notice it

criteria.title: Destructive actions grouped
criteria.description: Log out, delete account, and other irreversible actions in their own section at the bottom, visually distinguished in red

criteria.title: Account details at top
criteria.description: The user's avatar, name, and email shown prominently at the top of settings, a clear anchor for whose account is being managed

criteria.title: Deep link to specific settings
criteria.description: A direct link from relevant in-app prompts to the specific settings screen they reference — notification preferences, privacy, and so on.
criteria.suggestion: Telling users where to find a setting is far less effective than linking them there directly.

criteria.title: Support and feedback access
criteria.description: A clear path to contact support, submit feedback, or access help documentation, accessible from within settings.

criteria.title: App version
criteria.description: The current app version shown at the bottom of settings — essential for support conversations and identifying build-specific issues.

criteria.title: Legal links
criteria.description: Links to the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service accessible within settings, as required by app stores.

checklists.name: Splash Screen
checklists.description: The first screen a user sees when launching the mobile app and it initialises before transitioning to the home screen.

criteria.title: Logo or wordmark
criteria.description: The app brand mark centred on a clean background

criteria.title: Brand background
criteria.description: A solid or subtly branded background that makes the transition from the  mobile home screen clear

criteria.title: Launch duration
criteria.description: The splash visible only for as long as the app genuinely needs to initialise (not used as decorative padding)

criteria.title: Transition to first screen
criteria.description: A smooth, intentional animation into the first real screen, ideally not a hard cut or jarring flash

criteria.title: No interactive elements
criteria.description: The splash screen contains no buttons, inputs, or tappable areas, it is purely for transition

criteria.title: Loading indicator
criteria.description: For any initialisation taking more than a second so the user knows something is happening
criteria.suggestion: This could be your logo, wordmark or illustration you use as the key visual in a looping animation

checklists.name: Tab Bar Navigation
checklists.description: The persistent bottom navigation bar that gives users access to the top-level sections of the app

criteria.title: Tab count
criteria.description: Limited to the most important destinations — 3 to 5 items is the typical range
criteria.suggestion: More than 5 sections dilutes each option and may not fit

criteria.title: Icon and label
criteria.description: Each tab paired with both an icon and a text label
criteria.suggestion: Labels may not be necessary but only if icons are explicitly clear at what lies within that section

criteria.title: Active and default states
criteria.description: Active should be visually distinct whether it's colour, border or icon weight

criteria.title: Badge counts
criteria.description: Useful for tabs with unread counts like messages and notifications, updating in real time
criteria.suggestion: Instead of a number, a dot is suitable if numbers feels less relevant

criteria.title: Fixed presence
criteria.description: For the sections the tab bar applies to, tab bar should remain visible, and can be hidden on any page a level deeper

criteria.title: Tap target size
criteria.description: Each tab at least 44×44pt to be reliably tappable with a thumb in any grip position

criteria.title: Haptic feedback
criteria.description: A subtle tap haptic on tab selection confirming the action

criteria.title: Item list
criteria.description: Each item in the cart shown with its image, name, selected variants, and quantity

criteria.title: Quantity stepper
criteria.description: Plus and minus controls for adjusting quantity inline that are large enough to tap accurately without zooming.

criteria.title: Swipe to remove
criteria.description: A swipe-left gesture on a cart item revealing a remove action to delete item

criteria.title: Price breakdown
criteria.description: Subtotal, any applied discounts, estimated tax, and total shown before the checkout action.
criteria.suggestion: If prices will change after cart e.g. delivery fee, specify that it will be shown later

criteria.title: Empty cart state
criteria.description: The state shown when no items are in the cart, with a clear prompt to continue browsing

criteria.title: Promo code field
criteria.description: The ability to enter the code and see discount across items and total
criteria.suggestion: Can also be visible at checkout, but users may want to see the discounts here first before proceeding

checklists.name: Login
checklists.description: Everything a returning user needs to authenticate quickly and securely.

criteria.title: Social sign-in
criteria.description: Sign-in options that connect to an existing Apple or Google account, bypassing manual credential entry.
criteria.suggestion: On iOS, Apple Sign In is required by App Store guidelines if any other social provider is offered.

criteria.title: Email field
criteria.description: The input where users enter the email address associated with their account.

criteria.title: Password field
criteria.description: A masked text input for the account password, with the option to reveal what has been typed.

criteria.title: Biometric authentication
criteria.description: Face ID or fingerprint sign-in for returning users who have already authenticated once with a password
criteria.suggestion: Encouraged to suggest after initial login so it’s a faster experience in the future

criteria.title: Credential autofill
criteria.description: System-level support for pre-filling saved email and password from the user's password manager.
criteria.suggestion: textContentType on iOS and autoComplete on Android are the attributes that trigger native autofill.

criteria.title: Forgot password link
criteria.description: The link users reach for when they can't recall their password, leading into the reset flow.

criteria.title: Error states
criteria.description: Feedback shown when authentication fails, distinguishing between an unrecognised email address and an incorrect password.
criteria.suggestion: Generic 'incorrect credentials' gives users no useful signal — knowing whether the email or password is wrong helps them recover without guessing.

criteria.title: Passwordless sign-in (magic link)
criteria.description: An alternative sign-in method that sends a one-time link to the user's email, requiring no password
criteria.suggestion: Useful for infrequent-use apps where remembering a password between sessions is difficult

checklists.name: Account
checklists.description: Private account settings like credentials, linked accounts, notifications, and destructive actions.

criteria.title: Email
criteria.description: The current email address displayed with an option to update it
criteria.suggestion: Verifying the new address before completing the change is standard practice, where notifying the old address too adds a useful security signal.

criteria.title: Password change
criteria.description: A way for users to update their account password.
criteria.suggestion: Requiring the current password before accepting a new one prevents unauthorised changes on an unlocked device

criteria.title: Linked accounts
criteria.description: A view of which third-party accounts are connected for sign-in or data access, with ability to disconnect

criteria.title: Save confirmation
criteria.description: Clear feedback that changes have been saved, either inline or as a toast
criteria.suggestion: Auto-save with a subtle confirmation is more pleasant than explicit save, but if you want an explicit save button, it should remain disabled until there are changes

criteria.title: Delete or deactivate account
criteria.description: Options to deactivate or permanently delete the account, clearly separated from other settings

checklists.name: Invite
checklists.description: The flow for adding collaborators or members to a shared space with role assignment and pending invite management.

criteria.title: Email invite
criteria.description: The primary method of inviting someone by entering their email address directly

criteria.title: Role or permission selection
criteria.description: A control for setting what the invited person will be able to see and do once they accept
criteria.suggestion: Show what each role can and cannot do before the invite is sent, since this prevents over-permissioning and the back-and-forth of revoking access later. Keep roles to three or fewer where possible

criteria.title: Contact picker
criteria.description: Access to the device's contacts list for finding people to invite without typing a full address
criteria.suggestion: On iOS this requires explicit permission. Prime the user with a custom screen before the system prompt, since 'Find people you already know' performs better than asking cold

criteria.title: Bulk invite
criteria.description: A way to add multiple people at once, by entering several addresses or pasting a list
criteria.suggestion: Support comma-separated and line-break-separated input, since users are likely to paste from spreadsheets or threads

criteria.title: Pending invites + actions
criteria.description: A list of sent invitations that have not yet been accepted, with the option to resend or revoke each one
criteria.suggestion: Show when each invite was sent and when it expires for context on most recent invite sent

criteria.title: Shareable invite link
criteria.description: A link that grants access to anyone who opens it, with a configurable permission level
criteria.suggestion: Include an expiry option and a usage limit on the link for security

criteria.title: Seat or member limit
criteria.description: A visible count of remaining available seats, surfaced before the user reaches the plan's member cap

criteria.title: Access scope summary
criteria.description: A clear statement of what the invited person will be able to see and do, shown to the sender before confirming

checklists.name: 2FA
checklists.description: A screen that guides users through setting up or completing two-factor authentication to add a second layer of security to their account

criteria.title: Method selection
criteria.description: Authenticator app, SMS, or email code
criteria.suggestion: Offer at least 2 methods as some users potentially don't have access to one or the other

criteria.title: Setup instructions
criteria.description: Clear step-by-step guidance for completing setup, particularly for authenticator flows that require scanning a QR code

criteria.title: QR code or setup key
criteria.description: A scannable QR code or copyable key for linking an authenticator app to the account
criteria.suggestion: Ensure QR code size large enough to be easy to scan

criteria.title: Verification step
criteria.description: A code entry step confirming the setup was successful before 2FA is enabled on the account
criteria.suggestion: Enabling 2FA without this step risks a silent setup failure that locks the user out — a serious support burden

criteria.title: Recovery codes
criteria.description: A set of one-time backup codes the user can use if they lose access to their 2FA method
criteria.suggestion: Make download or copying the code a required step before completing setup for the sake of the user

criteria.title: Setup confirmation
criteria.description: A clear success state confirming that 2FA is now active on the account

criteria.title: Disable or reset option
criteria.description: A way for users to turn off or reconfigure 2FA, accessible from account security settings
criteria.suggestion: Re-authentication should be required before disabling 2FA

checklists.name: Account
checklists.description: Where users view and manage their personal information, preferences, and account-level details

criteria.title: Profile photo
criteria.description: A way for users to upload or change their profile image
criteria.suggestion: Consider a sensible fallback like initials or a placeholder icon for users who haven't uploaded a photo so a profile image still exists

criteria.title: Display name
criteria.description: The name shown to other users or across the product interface e.g. username, email address, first and last name
criteria.suggestion: Worth clarifying whether this is a public-facing name or an internal account label

criteria.title: Account details
criteria.description: Fields for email address, phone number, job title, or other relevant identifying information based on the product and information collected
criteria.suggestion: If the information becomes extensive, it's suitable to group e.g. contact information, job history

criteria.title: Linked accounts (if applicable)
criteria.description: A view of which third-party accounts are connected for sign-in or data access, with ability to disconnect

criteria.title: Save confirmation
criteria.description: Clear feedback that changes have been saved, either inline or as a toast
criteria.suggestion: Auto-save with a subtle confirmation is more pleasant than explicit save, but if you want an explicit save button, it should remain disabled until there are changes

criteria.title: Delete or deactivate account
criteria.description: Options to deactivate or permanently delete the account, clearly separated from other settings

checklists.name: Admin Panel
checklists.description: Where administrators manage users, configure the product, and oversee activity across the organisation

criteria.title: Role-based access
criteria.description: The admin panel visible and accessible only to users with the appropriate permissions

criteria.title: User management
criteria.description: A view of all users in the organisation with the ability to invite, edit roles, and remove members

criteria.title: Organisation settings
criteria.description: Controls for configuring the product at an account level — name, logo, SSO, domains

criteria.title: Usage overview
criteria.description: High-level metrics on how the product is being used across the organisation, with ability to export information for reporting

criteria.title: Billing and plan management
criteria.description: Access to subscription details, seat counts, and invoices at the account level

criteria.title: Audit log
criteria.description: A record of account related actions taken by users e.g. logins, permission changes, deletions

criteria.title: Danger zone
criteria.description: Destructive account-level actions e.g. deleting the workspace, transferring ownership
criteria.suggestion: Establish friction by visually separated this from other settings and having typed confirmation for irreversible actions

checklists.name: API Keys
checklists.description: A screen where users generate and manage API keys and other developer-facing credentials needed to integrate the product programmatically.

criteria.title: Key list
criteria.description: A table of all existing API keys showing name, creation date, last used date, and permissions
criteria.suggestion: Only show the last few characters after creation for identification without risk of revealing entire key

criteria.title: Generate key
criteria.description: A clear way to create a new API key, with the option to give it a name and set its scope or permissions
criteria.suggestion: Unnamed keys become impossible to manage as the list grows, so requiring a name before generation is useful

criteria.title: Copy key on creation
criteria.description: The full key revealed exactly once immediately after creation, with a prominent copy button
criteria.suggestion: Users need to be explicitly told this is the only time the key will be shown in full, following this it will be impossible to copy again

criteria.title: Key permissions or scopes
criteria.description: The ability to limit what each key can access (read-only, specific resources, or full access)
criteria.suggestion: Least-privilege access is a security best practice, and when fine-grained scopes are easier to set than full-access, more users choose them

criteria.title: Revoke key
criteria.description: A clear way to immediately invalidate a key, with a confirmation step before proceeding.
criteria.suggestion: Revocation is instant and irreversible, so the confirmation message needs to communicate this clearly, since there is no undo

criteria.title: Documentation link
criteria.description: A direct link to API documentation so developers can get started without having to search for it

checklists.name: Billing
checklists.description: Payment methods, invoices, and everything related to the financial side of the account

criteria.title: Payment method on file
criteria.description: The current card or payment method linked to the account, shown with masked details
criteria.suggestion: Last 4 digits of card are enough for the user to identify which card is in use without exposing sensitive information

criteria.title: Add or update payment method action
criteria.description: A way to enter a new card or change the current one

criteria.title: Next billing date and amount
criteria.description: When the next payment will be taken and for how much
criteria.suggestion: Including the plan name alongside the amount if applicable

criteria.title: Invoices and receipts
criteria.description: A list of past charges with the ability to download a PDF invoice for each.
criteria.suggestion: Ensure invoices include company name, address, and VAT number — legally required in many countries and a frequent request from business users.

criteria.title: Tax and VAT (if applicable)
criteria.description: Applicable tax or VAT shown on invoices and billing history

criteria.title: Failed payment recovery
criteria.description: Clear messaging and recovery instructions when a payment attempt has failed
criteria.suggestion: Surface this issue prominently in the app as it can eventually restrict access if not resolve in time

criteria.title: Billing contact email
criteria.description: The email address where invoices and billing notifications are sent
criteria.suggestion: For larger teams, this is often different from the account owner's email

checklists.name: Chat
checklists.description: A screen for real-time or asynchronous messaging between users, either one-on-one or in a group context.

criteria.title: Message thread
criteria.description: A chronological display of messages in the conversation, with the most recent at the bottom
criteria.suggestion: Auto-scrolling to the latest message on load is expected, but scrolling up to read history should never be interrupted by new messages arriving

criteria.title: Message input
criteria.description: A text field for composing and sending messages, with support for multi-line input
criteria.suggestion: Multi-line input is often defined with Shift + Enter, with just Enter alone triggering the message to be sent

criteria.title: Sender identification
criteria.description: The sender's name and avatar displayed alongside each message, making the conversation easy to follow
criteria.suggestion: Consecutive messages from the same sender typically don't need repeated name and avatar, so grouping them reduces visual clutter

criteria.title: Timestamps
criteria.description: When each message was sent, using relative time for recent messages and a full timestamp for older ones

criteria.title: Read receipts
criteria.description: An indicator showing whether the other participant has seen a message.
criteria.suggestion: Not all users want this level of visibility into their activity — read receipts are worth making optional where the product allows.

criteria.title: File and media sharing
criteria.description: The ability to attach images, files, or links within the conversation, and show those attachments within the conversation

criteria.title: Reactions
criteria.description: Emoji reactions on individual messages as a lightweight way to respond without sending a full reply

criteria.title: Anchor to context
criteria.description: Comments attached to a specific piece of content (a paragraph, image, task, or row) rather than floating in a general thread

criteria.title: Reply threading
criteria.description: Replies nested under the comment they respond to, keeping related discussion together without flattening into a chronological list

criteria.title: Resolve and archive (if applicable)
criteria.description: A way to mark a comment thread as resolved, removing it from the active view while keeping it accessible in a history or resolved state

criteria.title: Reactions
criteria.description: Emoji reactions on individual comments as a lightweight way to acknowledge without adding a reply

criteria.title: @mention element
criteria.description: Mentioning a user by name notifying them directly, drawing them into the thread without requiring a separate message
criteria.suggestion: Visually distinguish this so it's clear when a user is mentioned vs their name just being written in plain text

criteria.title: Edit action
criteria.description: The ability to edit a comment after posting, with a visible edited marker for transparency after saving edit

criteria.title: Delete action
criteria.description: Ability to delete a comment after posting, with a confirmation modal beforehand

criteria.title: Comment count indicator
criteria.description: A visible count or badge on the item being discussed, so collaborators can see where active threads exist without opening each one

checklists.name: Empty State
checklists.description: The state of a screen or component when there is no data to display, whether it's because a user is new, has cleared their content, or a search returned no results.

criteria.title: Illustration or icon
criteria.description: A visual that signals the empty state and gives the screen some personality, rather than feeling broken
criteria.suggestion: Visual should be contextual e.g. empty inbox and a deleted account shouldn't be the same

criteria.title: Clear heading
criteria.description: A short, plain-language title naming what's missing
criteria.suggestion: 'It's empty' isn't helpful while 'No projects yet' is clear

criteria.title: Supporting description
criteria.description: A brief explanation of what belongs in this space, most useful for first-time users

criteria.title: Primary action
criteria.description: A CTA pointing toward the next step: creating, importing, connecting etc
criteria.suggestion: It should create the first item, not just link somewhere generic

criteria.title: Zero state vs. no-results state
criteria.description: A distinction between a screen that is empty because nothing has been created versus one that returned no search or filter results
criteria.suggestion: A no-results state without a way to reset or broaden the search is a dead end — always provide an escape route

criteria.title: Error state variant
criteria.description: A separate variant for when content failed to load, as opposed to genuinely being empty
criteria.suggestion: Showing an empty state when the real issue is a loading error causes users to assume they have lost their data

checklists.name: Feed
checklists.description: A stream of content, activity, or updates that users scroll through to stay informed.

criteria.title: Feed item preview
criteria.description: A preview of each feed item (title, excerpt, or thumbnail) sufficient to judge whether the item is worth opening
criteria.suggestion: Variable-height items force the eye to re-adjust between each card whereas a consistent layout makes items harder to differentiate

criteria.title: Author
criteria.description: The name and avatar of the person who created or posted each item
criteria.suggestion: Linking the author name to their profile is a natural interaction expectation in most social or collaborative contexts

criteria.title: Timestamps
criteria.description: When each item was published or last updated
criteria.suggestion: Relative time works well for recent items, but eventually it should switch to the exact date and time

criteria.title: Engagement actions
criteria.description: Ways to interact with feed items (like, comment, share, save, or react)
criteria.suggestion: Consider size of every interaction in terms of prominence and frequency of use

criteria.title: New content indicator
criteria.description: A banner or button that appears when new items have been posted since the user loaded the feed
criteria.suggestion: Auto-injecting new posts while the user is reading pushes existing content down and makes scrolling janky

criteria.title: Filtering
criteria.description: Controls for narrowing the feed to a specific category, content type, or followed accounts
criteria.suggestion: Always indicate when filters are active for users to understand why specific content may or may not be shown

criteria.title: Pagination or infinite scroll
criteria.description: A mechanism for loading more items as the user reaches the bottom of the feed
criteria.suggestion: Pagination is suited well for work-related apps that have extensive databases

criteria.title: Empty state
criteria.description: The state shown when the feed has no items to display whether due to no connections, no activity, or an empty filter result
criteria.suggestion: A first-use empty state can point towards a specific action e.g. follow people, create a post, invite a colleague

checklists.name: Help Center
checklists.description: A self-serve documentation hub where users can find answers without contacting support.

criteria.title: Search with suggestions
criteria.description: A prominent search input that returns relevant articles as the user types
criteria.suggestion: Autocomplete suggestions increase the chance of the user finding an answer quicker

criteria.title: Content categories
criteria.description: A hierarchy of topics that lets users browse when they are not sure what to search for
criteria.suggestion: Categories that reflect how users think about the product, not internal team structure, are what make browsing work

criteria.title: Featured and popular content
criteria.description: The most-viewed or most-useful articles surfaced on the help center homepage
criteria.suggestion: Popular articles shift as features change, so ensure featured content does not stay stale

criteria.title: Article formatting
criteria.description: Proper heading hierarchy, screenshots, and formatted code blocks in articles where relevant
criteria.suggestion: Screenshots become outdated quickly after redesigns, so a regular review process is critical

criteria.title: Last updated date
criteria.description: The date each article was last reviewed or edited, shown at the top.
criteria.suggestion: A recent date reaffirms the user that the content is up to date and valid to follow

criteria.title: Helpfulness feedback
criteria.description: A simple thumbs up/down or yes/no at the end of each article to help identify if content is not helpful and needs to be reconsidered

criteria.title: Related articles
criteria.description: Links to similar or adjacent articles that might answer follow-up questions

checklists.name: Integrations
checklists.description: A screen that shows the third-party tools and services a product can connect with, allowing users to link their existing workflows.

criteria.title: Catalogue
criteria.description: A browsable list or grid of all available integrations with logos, names, and a brief description of each
criteria.suggestion: Suggested to group later by installed and not installed after first integration is successfully connected

criteria.title: Categories or filtering
criteria.description: A way to browse integrations by category to narrow down a large catalogue (productivity, communication, analytics, CRM)

criteria.title: Search
criteria.description: A search field to find a specific integration by name without having to scroll through the full list

criteria.title: Connection status
criteria.description: A clear indicator on each integration showing whether it is connected, disconnected, or connected but is experiencing an issue
criteria.suggestion: A dot is better paired with a label if you want to be explicitly clear

criteria.title: Connect and disconnect actions
criteria.description: A clear way to initiate or remove a connection, with a confirmation step before disconnecting
criteria.suggestion: For disconnecting, include what will stop working in the confirmation step

criteria.title: Integration detail
criteria.description: A dedicated view for each integration showing what data it accesses, configuration options, and a sync or activity log.

criteria.title: Request an integration
criteria.description: A way for users to suggest tools they would like the product to support
criteria.suggestion: This doubles as a lightweight research tool as the most-requested integrations tell you exactly where to invest next.

checklists.name: Kanban board
checklists.description: A visual board that organises items into columns representing stages or statuses, allowing users to track and move work through a workflow.

criteria.title: Columns
criteria.description: Distinct vertical lanes representing each stage of the workflow (To Do, In Progress, Done, or custom stages)
criteria.suggestion: Every team structures their workflow differently, so adding, renaming, and reordering columns should be available

criteria.title: Cards
criteria.description: Individual items displayed within each column, showing the title and key metadata at a glance
criteria.suggestion: Title, assignee, and due date on the card face covers most use cases without cluttering

criteria.title: Drag and drop
criteria.description: The ability to move cards between columns and reorder them within a column by dragging
criteria.suggestion: A visual drop target as the card is dragged to indicate whereWithout it, users are never sure where the card will land

criteria.title: Quick add card
criteria.description: A fast way to create a new card directly within a column without opening a full form

criteria.title: Card detail on click
criteria.description: Clicking a card opening its full detail — description, comments, attachments, history — without leaving the board.
criteria.suggestion: Card detail in a side panel or modal rather than navigating away — losing the board context frustrates users.

criteria.title: Column item count
criteria.description: A count of how many cards are in each column, visible in the column header
criteria.suggestion: A count is useful for conversations and to keep track of column amount without individually counting items

criteria.title: Filtering, sorting and grouping
criteria.description: The ability to re-organise cards by assignee, label, priority, or due date to focus on a subset of work, as an example

checklists.name: Maintenance
checklists.description: A screen shown when the application is temporarily unavailable due to scheduled maintenance or an unexpected outage.

criteria.title: Clear status message
criteria.description: A plain-language explanation that the product is currently unavailable and why
criteria.suggestion: Scheduled maintenance and unexpected outages call for different messaging, since users respond very differently to each, and conflating them feels evasive

criteria.title: Estimated return time
criteria.description: When the product is expected to be back online, as specifically as possible
criteria.suggestion: Vague messages like 'back soon' frustrate users, since even a rough estimate like 'within 2 hours' is far more reassuring

criteria.title: Status page link
criteria.description: A link to a live status page where users can monitor progress and see real-time updates
criteria.suggestion: A status page hosted on a separate domain remains accessible even when your main infrastructure is down

criteria.title: Contact or support link
criteria.description: A way to reach support for urgent issues that cannot wait for the maintenance window to end

criteria.title: Brand consistency
criteria.description: A maintenance page styled consistently with the product, even if the content is minimal
criteria.suggestion: A well-designed maintenance page communicates professionalism and reduces user anxiety

checklists.name: Multi-step form
checklists.description: A form split across multiple steps or screens to reduce cognitive load when collecting a large amount of information from the user.

criteria.title: Progress indicator
criteria.description: A clear visual showing how many steps exist and which one the user is currently on
criteria.suggestion: Labels for each step help give context hint to future steps

criteria.title: Step heading and context
criteria.description: A clear title and brief context for each step, so users know what they are being asked to provide.

criteria.title: Field grouping
criteria.description: Each step containing only fields that belong together logically e.g. phone and email for contact details

criteria.title: Step-level validation
criteria.description: Validation happening at each step before the user proceeds, not surfaced all at once at the end

criteria.title: Back navigation
criteria.description: The ability to return to a previous step to review or change answers without losing subsequent progress

criteria.title: Save and resume
criteria.description: The ability to save progress and return to the form later
criteria.suggestion: Particularly useful for forms that require information that connect be instantly provided or sourced

criteria.title: Final review step
criteria.description: A summary of all entered information before final submission, giving the user a chance to review and edit
criteria.suggestion: Offer a link to each section on at this step for editing

checklists.name: Notification Settings
checklists.description: Where users configure exactly which notifications they receive, through which channels, and how frequently.

criteria.title: Categories
criteria.description: Notification types organised into logical groups e.g. product activity, mentions, billing, security, marketing

criteria.title: Channel selection
criteria.description: Controls for which channel each notification type comes through e.g. in-app, email, push, or SMS
criteria.suggestion: Not all channels make sense for all notification types — a billing alert via push notification is rarely necessary

criteria.title: Frequency controls
criteria.description: Where applicable, controls for how often notifications arrive e.g. immediately, daily digest, or weekly summary.

criteria.title: Global mute
criteria.description: A way to temporarily silence all notifications without having to turn each one off individually

criteria.title: Save confirmation
criteria.description: A clear indication that preference changes have been saved.
criteria.suggestion: Auto-save works well also, the key thing is ensuring the user is aware the changes are enabled as often they are customising due to preference or annoyance

checklists.name: Notifications
checklists.description: An area that surfaces alerts, updates, and activity relevant to the user to help them stay informed

criteria.title: Notification list
criteria.description: A chronological feed of alerts, messages, and activity updates for the user.
criteria.suggestion: Date grouping (today, yesterday, this week) makes the list more scannable

criteria.title: Read and unread states
criteria.description: A clear visual distinction between notifications the user has and hasn't seen
criteria.suggestion: An unread count can also appear on the icon/button that opens notifications

criteria.title: Notification type
criteria.description: A visual or label indicating type e.g. mention, system alert, billing event

criteria.title: Timestamp
criteria.description: A relative time for recent items e.g. 2 mins ago, a complete date and time for older ones e.g. May 14 7:08pm

criteria.title: Actions (if applicable)
criteria.description: An action related to the notification event e.g. a notification that involves a direct message could have a 'reply' button

criteria.title: Mark all as read
criteria.description: A single action to clear all unread indicators at once

criteria.title: Empty state
criteria.description: A clear message when there are no notifications

checklists.name: Onboarding
checklists.description: A guided experience that introduces new users to the product and gets them to their first moment of value as quickly as possible

criteria.title: Progress indicator
criteria.description: An indication of how many steps are involved and where the user currently is in the sequence
criteria.suggestion: Every step beyond five is another opportunity to lose the user — 3 to 5 is the reliable range

criteria.title: Welcome message
criteria.description: A brief message acknowledging this is a new experience and orienting the user toward what the product does.

criteria.title: Account setup
criteria.description: The minimum information needed to personalise the experience, gathered at the start
criteria.suggestion: Delay any fields not genuinely needed to start using the product

criteria.title: Product highlights
criteria.description: Key features introduced through short contextual tips or a visual walkthrough
criteria.suggestion: Offer a skip route for user who has seen content before or prefers to learn by doing

criteria.title: First action prompt
criteria.description: A clear prompt directing the user to an action or feature
criteria.suggestion: This should be the quickest step towards a user understanding the value of the product

criteria.title: Completion confirmation
criteria.description: A clear acknowledgement that setup is complete, transitioning the user into the main product

checklists.name: Public Profile
checklists.description: The view of a user that other people in the product see, distinct from the account settings profile, which is private and editable.

criteria.title: Avatar and display name
criteria.description: The user's photo and name, shown prominently as the primary identifier on the profile
criteria.suggestion: A fallback avatar using initials is better than a blank space

criteria.title: Role or title
criteria.description: The user's job title, team, or role within the product context, where relevant

criteria.title: Bio or description
criteria.description: A short free-text description the user has written about themselves

criteria.title: Activity or contributions
criteria.description: A summary of what the user has done in the product (posts, projects, comments, or other public actions)
criteria.suggestion: Surfacing activity the user hasn't chosen to make public is a privacy violation, since public profiles should only reflect what the user has explicitly opted in to show

criteria.title: Contact or follow action
criteria.description: A way to initiate contact, follow, or connect with the user, depending on what the product supports

criteria.title: Joined date (optional)
criteria.description: When the user joined the product

criteria.title: Profile visibility controls
criteria.description: Which profile fields are visible according to the user's own privacy preferences

checklists.name: Search Results
checklists.description: Displaying and navigating results matching a user's query from within the product.

criteria.title: Search input
criteria.description: A search field at the top of the results, pre-filled with the current query so it can be refined without starting over

criteria.title: Result count
criteria.description: How many results were found for the query
criteria.suggestion: Show it even at zero as it tells the user the search ran, not that something broke

criteria.title: Result items
criteria.description: Each result shown with enough to identify it — title, type, image, and a snippet of the matching content
criteria.suggestion: Highlighting the matched term in the snippet confirms

criteria.title: Result type indicators
criteria.description: A label or icon marking what kind of item each result is (document, person, project, message)

criteria.title: Filters
criteria.description: The ability to narrow results by category, date, status, or other relevant values

criteria.title: No results state
criteria.description: The state shown when a query returns no matches, ideally with suggestions for what to try instead
criteria.suggestion: Offer alternatives instead of a blank space, whether it's a suggested query or spelling change

criteria.title: Recent searches
criteria.description: A list of the user's previous queries, shown when the search field is focused but empty

checklists.name: Settings
checklists.description: A screen that gives users control over their account, preferences, and application behaviour

criteria.title: Structure
criteria.description: Organising settings controls into logical categories e.g. account, notifications, security, billing.
criteria.suggestion: Consider elevating the most commonly changed settings rather than the most important

criteria.title: Account details
criteria.description: The fields where users update their name, email address, and profile photo

criteria.title: Security details
criteria.description: The ability to change the password,  two-factor authentication and other security information
criteria.suggestion: These fields should require re-authentication to save changes

criteria.title: Notification preferences
criteria.description: Controls for which notifications the user receives and through which channel, grouped by type (product updates, reminders, billing)
criteria.suggestion: Grouping by type and/or platform helps reduce the chances of a user disabling all notifications rather than some

criteria.title: Billing
criteria.description: Managing payment method, upgrading or cancelling a payment — this could also be a preview of this information with a link directly to the billing page if separate

criteria.title: Additional preferences (if applicable)
criteria.description: Language, timezone, date format, and appearance settings like dark mode

criteria.title: Danger zone
criteria.description: Destructive actions like account deletion, clearly separated from the rest of settings
criteria.suggestion: Include a confirmation step for any destructive actions, with details on what will be lost if the user continues

checklists.name: Single Item Detail
checklists.description: A screen that displays the full details of a single record — a user, order, document, or any other entity — after selecting it from a list.

criteria.title: Clear title or identifier
criteria.description: The name, ID, or primary label of the item, shown prominently at the top of the screen

criteria.title: Status indicator (if applicable)
criteria.description: A clear signal of the item's current state (active, pending, completed, archived)
criteria.suggestion: Colour-blind users can't distinguish status by colour alone, so include a text label alongside the colour indicator to ensure it's readable

criteria.title: Key details section
criteria.description: The most important attributes of the item surfaced prominently, with secondary details available below or in a sidebar
criteria.suggestion: It’s critical to exercise hierarchy here and consider what details matter more than others, and how can they be effectively grouped

criteria.title: Edit action
criteria.description: A clear way to modify the item's details, either inline or via an edit mode

criteria.title: Related items or activity
criteria.description: Associated records, linked content, or a history of changes related to this item
criteria.suggestion: An activity log showing who did what and when is highly valued in collaborative products

criteria.title: Breadcrumb or back navigation
criteria.description: A way to return to the list or parent context

criteria.title: Destructive actions
criteria.description: Delete or archive options, available on the detail screen but kept visually separate from the primary actions

checklists.name: Timeline / Gantt View
checklists.description: A screen that displays tasks, milestones, or events along a horizontal time axis, commonly used in project management products to show schedules and dependencies.

criteria.title: Time axis
criteria.description: A horizontal axis representing time, with clear date markers (days, weeks, or months depending on the zoom level)
criteria.suggestion: A timeline locked to a single timescale rarely fits all project sizes, and zoom controls let users shift between day, week, and month views as needed

criteria.title: Task bars
criteria.description: Horizontal bars representing each task or milestone, positioned according to their start and end dates
criteria.suggestion: A monochrome timeline becomes hard to parse at a glance — colouring bars by status, assignee, or category makes patterns visible immediately

criteria.title: Dependencies
criteria.description: Visual connectors between tasks that must be completed in sequence, showing which items are blocked by others
criteria.suggestion: Dependency lines can visually overwhelm a busy timeline, so showing them on hover or when a task is selected keeps the default view readable

criteria.title: Today indicator
criteria.description: A vertical line marking the current date so users can immediately see what is on track and what is overdue

criteria.title: Milestones
criteria.description: Distinct markers for key dates or deliverables that are not duration-based tasks

criteria.title: Drag to reschedule
criteria.description: The ability to move or resize task bars by dragging to update dates directly on the timeline
criteria.suggestion: A date tooltip while dragging gives users precise feedback on the new start and end dates

criteria.title: Row grouping
criteria.description: The ability to organise tasks by assignee, team, project phase, or another dimension

checklists.name: User Management
checklists.description: A screen that allows admins to view, invite, and manage the users who have access to a product or workspace.

criteria.title: User list
criteria.description: A table of all users showing name, email, role, and account status
criteria.suggestion: Activity information is also useful to show here to help spotlight inactive users

criteria.title: Invite user action
criteria.description: A clear way to add new members by email, with an option to set their role before sending
criteria.suggestion: Depending on your average user team size, a bulk invite action is valuable to include and a common way for teams to transfer a company user base from another product

criteria.title: Roles and permissions
criteria.description: The ability to assign and change what each user can see and do within the product
criteria.suggestion: Stick with universal terms like admin, member or viewer where possible, avoiding custom user titles

criteria.title: Pending invitation status
criteria.description: A view of invitations sent but not yet accepted, with the option to resend or revoke

criteria.title: Search and filter
criteria.description: The ability to find users quickly by name, email, role or other additional user information that applies

criteria.title: Remove or deactivate user
criteria.description: A clear way to revoke access, with a distinction between temporary deactivation and permanent removal

checklists.name: Version History
checklists.description: A screen outlining different versions of an item or experience that you can navigate between.

criteria.title: Version timeline
criteria.description: A list of saved versions in reverse chronological order, each labelled with a timestamp and the user who saved it

criteria.title: Named versions
criteria.description: The ability to give a version a name (a milestone, a submission date, a phase label) so it is findable without scrolling through timestamps
criteria.suggestion: Autosave versions are useful for recovery, but named versions are what users actually navigate by, so making both available covers both use cases

criteria.title: Version preview
criteria.description: A read-only preview of any past version, visible without committing to a restore

criteria.title: Diff or change summary
criteria.description: A visual indication of what changed between two versions (added, removed, or modified content)
criteria.suggestion: A diff view reduces the time it takes to evaluate whether a version is the right one to restore

criteria.title: Restore action
criteria.description: A clear way to make a past version the current one, with a confirmation step that sets expectations about what will happen to the current content

criteria.title: Autosave indicator
criteria.description: A persistent, subtle indicator of when the document was last saved automatically, visible without being disruptive

checklists.name: Pricing
checklists.description: A pricing page breaks down costs, features and options for paying to access the product itself or a version of it.

criteria.title: Plan names, prices and frequency
criteria.description: The name and cost of each available plan, with billing frequency clearly stated

criteria.title: Billing period toggle
criteria.description: A switch between monthly and annual billing, with the annual discount shown if applicable

criteria.title: Feature comparison (if price options)
criteria.description: A side-by-side breakdown of what each plan includes and excludes

criteria.title: Call to action
criteria.description: A button on each plan to start a trial, subscribe, or contact sales

criteria.title: Free tier or trial details
criteria.description: What's included, how long it lasts, and what happens when it ends
criteria.suggestion: State clearly whether the account downgrades or charges automatically once the trial ends

criteria.title: FAQ section
criteria.description: Answers to the most common questions about billing, plan limits, cancellation, and payment

criteria.title: Enterprise option
criteria.description: A prompt for organisations that need a custom arrangement beyond the standard listed plans

checklists.name: Login
checklists.description: A login page is a critical component of many web applications, serving as the gateway for users to access personalized features, secure content, and their own data

criteria.title: Email and password fields
criteria.description: The two standard authentication inputs: an email address field and a password field.
criteria.suggestion: Pre-filling the email field after a failed login so the user only has to re-enter the password is a small detail that reduces friction

criteria.title: Show/hide password toggle
criteria.description: A button alongside the password field that reveals or conceals what the user has typed

criteria.title: Forgot password
criteria.description: A link that begins the password reset flow for users who cannot remember their credentials

criteria.title: Remember me
criteria.description: A checkbox that persists the user's session across browser closures

criteria.title: SSO or social login
criteria.description: Alternative authentication via a third-party identity provider (Google, Microsoft, GitHub) that bypasses the email/password form.

criteria.title: Sign up link
criteria.description: A link to the account creation screen for users who do not yet have an account

criteria.title: Error messages
criteria.description: Feedback shown when authentication fails, indicating what the user should try next

checklists.name: About
checklists.description: A page that tells the story of the company — who built it, why, and what they believe.

criteria.title: Origin story
criteria.description: A genuine account of why the company was founded and the problem it set out to solve

criteria.title: Mission or values
criteria.description: What the company stands for and how it makes decisions, stated plainly

criteria.title: Team
criteria.description: The people behind the product (names, roles, and faces) making the company feel human

criteria.title: Milestones or traction
criteria.description: Key moments in the company's history (founding year, customer count, notable launches) that establish credibility

criteria.title: Investors or backers
criteria.description: Logos or names of investors, accelerators, or notable backers, where relevant

criteria.title: CTA
criteria.description: A clear next step e.g. view open roles, read the blog, or try the product

checklists.name: Affiliate
checklists.description: A page that invites potential affiliates or partners to join a programme, explaining how it works and what they stand to earn.

criteria.title: Programme overview
criteria.description: A clear explanation of what the affiliate or partner programme involves and who it is designed for

criteria.title: Commission or reward structure
criteria.description: Exactly what affiliates earn (percentage, flat fee, recurring commission) stated plainly
criteria.suggestion: Ambiguous commission structures are the most common reason potential affiliates leave this page without applying

criteria.title: How it works
criteria.description: A simple step-by-step breakdown of joining, sharing, and earning
criteria.suggestion: If using a third party to connect, it's helpful to include screenshots for steps

criteria.title: Resources provided
criteria.description: What materials the company provides (links, banners, copy, tracking) to help affiliates succeed

criteria.title: Social proof
criteria.description: Testimonials or earnings examples from existing affiliates who are benefiting from the programme

criteria.title: Application or signup CTA
criteria.description: A clear form or button to join the programme

checklists.name: Billing
checklists.description: A screen where users manage information regarding payment, subscription and billing.

criteria.title: Payment method/s used
criteria.description: Display payment method details with ability to update or remove. A subscription service may want to prevent all methods being removed as it will become an issue later.

criteria.title: History
criteria.description: A list of past charges with the ability to download invoices
criteria.suggestion: Downloadable invoice format should be PDF to be easily shared in other reporting tools

criteria.title: Plan details
criteria.description: Details of current plan includes price, features and next billing date
criteria.suggestion: Have a clear action to upgrade or change plan in this area

criteria.title: Promo or discount code
criteria.description: A field to apply a code to activate a discount or deal

criteria.title: Additional details
criteria.description: Information that influences billing or plan decision making e.g. seats, roles, usage, metrics

criteria.title: Next payment
criteria.description: If subscription, show details of upcoming payment including amount, date and method

criteria.title: Cancel subscription
criteria.description: A clear action to cancel and stop payments

checklists.name: Compare
checklists.description: A page that positions the product directly against a specific competitor, helping prospects who are evaluating alternatives to make a decision.

criteria.title: Clear positioning statement
criteria.description: An opening that states plainly how this product differs from the competitor being compared
criteria.suggestion: A compare page that claims superiority on every dimension reads as untrustworthy so include honest acknowledgement of trade-offs for more credibility

criteria.title: Feature comparison table
criteria.description: A side-by-side table of key features showing what each product includes, with clear tick and cross indicators
criteria.suggestion:
This table focused on decision-relevant features 

This table doesn't have to mention every single feature, just the most persuasive and relevant to influencing decision

criteria.title: Key differentiators
criteria.description: A section expanding on the areas where this product genuinely excels beyond a table comparison

criteria.title: Social proof
criteria.description: Testimonials or quotes from customers who switched from the competitor being compared

criteria.title: Pricing comparison
criteria.description: A clear, fair comparison of pricing structures if the difference is a meaningful factor for prospects
criteria.suggestion: Pricing comparisons only work best if there's a genuine advantage e.g. cheaper or more value for money spent

criteria.title: CTA
criteria.description: A direct prompt to try the product or book a demo

checklists.name: Features
checklists.description: A page that walks through the full capabilities of the product, helping prospects understand what it does in depth.

criteria.title: Feature grouping
criteria.description: Capabilities organised into logical themes or categories so the page is scannable and not a wall of bullet points
criteria.suggestion: Features grouped by the job they help the user accomplish are easier to scan than those organised by how the product is built internally

criteria.title: Feature descriptions
criteria.description: Each feature explained in one or two sentences from the user's perspective, what they can do, not what the system does

criteria.title: Feature visuals
criteria.description: Screenshots, GIFs, or short video clips showing each feature in action
criteria.suggestion: For complex interactions, animated GIFs showing a feature in use can provide better storytelling and value than static screenshots

criteria.title: Benefits framing
criteria.description: Each feature connected explicitly to an outcome and/or benefit, not just the capability

criteria.title: Social proof per feature
criteria.description: A relevant customer quote placed alongside the feature it relates to, making the case more concrete.

criteria.title: CTA
criteria.description: A conversion point at the bottom and optionally inline throughout, for visitors who are convinced mid-page

checklists.name: Privacy
checklists.description: Page covering the legal terms of using the product (privacy policy, terms of service, and cookie policy) written clearly and kept current.

criteria.title: Privacy policy
criteria.description: A clear document explaining what data is collected, how it is used, how long it is kept, and how users can request deletion
criteria.suggestion: A plain-language summary at the top is an option, to allow most users understand the policy without diving into deeper details unless necessary

criteria.title: Terms of service
criteria.description: The agreement governing use of the product (user responsibilities, acceptable use, limitation of liability)

criteria.title: Cookie policy
criteria.description: A clear explanation of which cookies are used, what they do, and how users can control them
criteria.suggestion: Cookie policies separated from the privacy policy are increasingly what users search for, since they serve different functions and are regulated differently in most jurisdictions

criteria.title: Last updated date
criteria.description: A clear timestamp on every legal document so users know if they are reading the current version

criteria.title: Version history or changelog
criteria.description: For products with engaged users, a log of what changed between policy versions — builds trust and reduces enquiries.
criteria.suggestion: A summary of changes in plain English at the top of an updated policy is far more reassuring than just changing the date.

criteria.title: Contact for legal queries
criteria.description: A dedicated email or address for data, privacy, or legal enquiries as required by most regulations.

checklists.name: Press / Media
checklists.description: A page providing journalists, analysts, and content creators with the resources they need to cover the company accurately.

criteria.title: Company overview
criteria.description: A concise, factual description of the company, what it does, when it was founded, and who it serves
criteria.suggestion: A press overview written as a ready-to-use paragraph saves journalists time. The easier it is to lift and paste, the more often it gets used

criteria.title: Press coverage
criteria.description: A curated list of notable media mentions with publication name, headline, and link
