criteria.suggestion: Logos of well-known publications displayed visually signal credibility faster than a text list

criteria.title: Press contact
criteria.description: A dedicated email address for media enquiries so journalists know exactly where to reach the right person or team

criteria.title: Brand assets
criteria.description: Downloadable logos, product screenshots, and founder headshots in multiple formats
criteria.suggestion: Light and dark logo versions are both routinely needed by journalists, since a press kit without both creates unnecessary back-and-forth

criteria.title: Key statistics
criteria.description: Notable numbers that journalists can use to characterise the company e.g. customers, revenue milestones, countries, team size

criteria.title: Recent press releases
criteria.description: Archived official announcements for journalists researching the company's history

criteria.title: Certifications and compliance
criteria.description: Logos and names of security certifications held e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA
criteria.suggestion: Certification logos should be paired with an explanation of what they cover

criteria.title: Data encryption
criteria.description: A plain-language explanation of how data is encrypted at rest and in transit

criteria.title: Data residency
criteria.description: Where customer data is stored and processed, with any regional options available

criteria.title: Access controls
criteria.description: Who within the company can access customer data, under what conditions, and what controls are in place to limit that access

criteria.title: Vulnerability disclosure
criteria.description: How security issues are reported and handled e.g. a dedicated email address, a bug bounty programme, or a responsible disclosure policy

criteria.title: Incident history
criteria.description: A record of past security incidents that were disclosed, with dates and resolution summaries for transparency

criteria.title: Penetration testing
criteria.description: Details of third-party security audits or penetration tests, with the most recent date and ability to request a report for further details

criteria.title: Component status list
criteria.description: Each major service or component (API, dashboard, integrations, notifications) shown with its current operational state
criteria.suggestion: A single 'All systems operational' row on its own is less useful than per-component status, since users experiencing an issue with one part of the product need to know if it is on their end or yours

criteria.title: Live incident updates
criteria.description: During an active incident, timestamped updates posted in sequence (identifying the issue, confirming investigation, and reporting resolution)
criteria.suggestion: The cadence of updates matters more than their length — a brief 'investigating' post every 30 minutes is far more reassuring than silence followed by an explanation

criteria.title: Incident history
criteria.description: An archive of past incidents with dates, duration, affected components, and a brief post-mortem

criteria.title: Uptime metrics
criteria.description: Historical uptime percentages per component, typically covering a rolling 90-day window

criteria.title: Scheduled maintenance
criteria.description: Upcoming planned maintenance windows listed in advance with estimated duration and which components will be affected
criteria.suggestion: Scheduled maintenance announced at least 72 hours in advance (and communicated via the subscription channel) is far better absorbed than a surprise

criteria.title: Subscribe to updates
criteria.description: An email, SMS, or webhook subscription option so users are notified of incidents without having to check the page themselves

criteria.title: Separate domain
criteria.description: The status page hosted on a domain independent of the main infrastructure, so it remains accessible when the product itself is down
criteria.suggestion: A status page that goes offline during an outage is the single most common implementation failure. A separate hosting arrangement is the only reliable solution

checklists.name: Testimonials
checklists.description: A page dedicated to social proof, collecting customer quotes, reviews, and success stories in one place.

criteria.title: Customer quotes
criteria.description: Direct quotes from real customers describing their experience, attributed with name, role, and company
criteria.suggestion: Specific quotes that mention a concrete outcome are far more persuasive than generic praise ('It saved us 6 hours a week' beats 'Love this tool')

criteria.title: Customer details
criteria.description: Name, role, company, and photo for each testimonial, since anonymised quotes carry much less weight
criteria.suggestion: A recognisable company logo next to a quote multiplies its credibility significantly

criteria.title: Use case variety
criteria.description: Testimonials representing different customer types, industries, and use cases so visitors can find someone like them

criteria.title: Video testimonials
criteria.description: Short video clips from customers who are willing to speak on camera, for visitors who find video more convincing

criteria.title: Review platform badges
criteria.description: Aggregate scores from G2, Trustpilot, Capterra, or similar platforms linking to verified reviews
criteria.suggestion: Third-party review scores carry more weight than self-selected quotes, when scores are strong, lead with them

criteria.title: Email capture
criteria.description: A simple form (typically just an email field) to join the waitlist, with a clear statement of what joining means

criteria.title: What to expect
criteria.description: What waitlist members will receive (early access, a discount, a specific feature) and a rough timeline for when
criteria.suggestion: Vague waitlists that promise nothing specific generate sign-ups but very low activation when access eventually opens

criteria.title: Social proof
criteria.description: The total number of people already on the waitlist, displayed to signal demand and reduce the fear of backing something niche

criteria.title: Position indicator
criteria.description: The user's current position in the queue, shown after sign-up and updated as they move up
criteria.suggestion: Showing a specific position ('You are #847') is more motivating than a generic confirmation because it creates a concrete reference point to improve from

criteria.title: Referral mechanic
criteria.description: A shareable link that moves the user up the list when others join through it, incentivising organic sharing
criteria.suggestion: Referral waitlists consistently grow faster than static ones. The mechanic works because it aligns the user's interest with the product's growth

criteria.title: Progress toward access
criteria.description: An indication of how close the product is to general launch or how many spots remain at the current access tier

checklists.name: Team
checklists.description: A team page introduces an organization's staff members, leadership, or key personnel. It typically helps visitors understand the people behind the company while adding a human element to the brand's identity.

criteria.title: Personality and branding
criteria.description: A theme or tone that conveys how serious or funny your team behaves
criteria.suggestion: Colloquial copy helps you appears more accessible to users

criteria.title: Team members
criteria.description: A representation of your team, with amount of detail varying on the team size (8 people can be shown individually, but 800 not so much)

criteria.title: Visuals
criteria.description: Either photography or illustrations of the team, offices or culture

criteria.title: Group by area or team
criteria.description: Depending on your team size, you could divide the team members up by area (marketing, design, engineering) to allow an easier scan of members

criteria.title: Link to careers
criteria.description: After someone has seen who your team is and the culture, they may be interested in finding what job opportunities are available

criteria.title: Item name and image
criteria.description: Each item shown with its name and image, matching what was displayed on the product page.

criteria.title: Update or remove item
criteria.description: The ability to adjust quantity, change variants, or remove an item directly from the cart.

criteria.title: Item variations
criteria.description: Selected variants for each item — size, colour, style, or type — displayed clearly alongside the item.
criteria.suggestion: A mismatch between what the user selected and what appears in the cart is a common source of disputes — the variant should always be clearly visible.

criteria.title: Promo or discount code
criteria.description: A text field for entering a promo, discount, or coupon code.
criteria.suggestion: Showing whether the code was accepted or rejected immediately after entry removes any ambiguity.

criteria.title: Accepted payment methods
criteria.description: The payment methods available for completing the purchase — cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, and others.
criteria.suggestion: Displaying recognised payment method logos increases trust at the most anxious point of the purchase flow.

criteria.title: Link to support
criteria.description: A way to get help with items in the cart — particularly useful for products with configurable options or custom orders.

criteria.title: Checkout button
criteria.description: A prominent button to proceed to payment when the user is ready to complete their order.

criteria.title: Suggested add-ons
criteria.description: Related or complementary items suggested based on what is already in the cart.

checklists.name: Search
checklists.description: A search results page displays organized findings based on a user's search query. It presents relevant matches in a scannable view to help users quickly find and navigate to their desired destination.

criteria.title: Search box
criteria.description: The element a user types in to make a search
criteria.suggestion: A search box should be at the top of the page, styled consistently with other search boxes across your website or product Include a button to click to process search Placeholder text can nudge the user to make a relevant search

criteria.title: Visualisation of results
criteria.description: Showing the items relevant to the search
criteria.suggestion: Give as much detail as you can to contextualize the results e.g. show the title of the page, a description and potentially a thumbnail Show the number of results Include pagination for long list of results (more than 50) If there are no results, point the user towards making another search or another pathway

criteria.title: Search progress
criteria.description: A search may not be instant, so consider a loading indicator as the product makes the enquiry

criteria.title: Suggested search items
criteria.description: Offer a search query to save the user from typing e.g. currently trending, most popular, recently search, autocorrection

criteria.title: Categories and/or filters
criteria.description: Constraints to help users narrow down their search area

criteria.title: Ordering of search results
criteria.description: How a user can sort results e.g. best price, most relevant, newest first

criteria.title: Highlighting keywords
criteria.description: Highlight the words in the search enquiry within the results displayed

checklists.name: Careers
checklists.description: A careers page typically displays job openings, company culture, and employment opportunities. It allows potential candidates to explore available positions, learn about the organization's values, and typically includes functionality to submit job applications or contact recruiters.

criteria.title: Company story
criteria.description: Share how the business started off and the journey it has experienced
criteria.suggestion: Don't just share the what, but the why and motivations behind the foundation

criteria.title: Up to date information
criteria.description: Ensure all the content is up to date, especially quantitative values e.g. team headcount, offices open, time operating

criteria.title: Employee benefits
criteria.description: Perks and value props for potential employees
criteria.suggestion: Ensure the benefits show real, tangible value and aren't gimmicks

criteria.title: Teams and divisions
criteria.description: Either a breakdown of the team members or what areas you currently have
criteria.suggestion: Determine the amount of information based on the team size - a bio and links can be featured for a team of 10, but may not work for a team of 200+

criteria.title: Job openings
criteria.description: A listing of all roles currently available to apply for
criteria.suggestion: Break up the roles by department for easier scanning

criteria.title: Working locations
criteria.description: Showcase where your offices are, and if you offer remote work

criteria.title: Employee testimonials
criteria.description: Feature stories from current employees that share why they love working at the company and what someone can expect

checklists.name: Blog Post
checklists.description: A blog post page displays a single article's content, including its title, author, publication date, and body text. It often includes related media (images, videos), social sharing options, and commenting functionality, allowing readers to engage with the content and navigate to other posts.

criteria.title: Title
criteria.description: Copy that educates the user on what to expect to read, typically phrased in an eye-catching or interesting manner

criteria.title: Sub heading
criteria.description: Elaborating on the title, defining the purpose of the post

criteria.title: Thumbnail
criteria.description: A visual aid to illustrate the themes of the content
criteria.suggestion: Thumbnail style should draw from branding and style guide

criteria.title: Author
criteria.description: Who wrote and contributed to the post
criteria.suggestion: Make an author's profile selectable to let users follow their favourite writers in the blog

criteria.title: Content
criteria.description: The actual blog post itself
criteria.suggestion: Consider responsiveness and how content is represented on smaller devices

criteria.title: Social sharing tools
criteria.description: Ability to share or send the post to other people
criteria.suggestion: Positioning this element in a fixed position on the page allows the opportunity for the user to share the post at any point

criteria.title: Lead conversion content
criteria.description: Introducing relevant information about your product that ties in with the post

criteria.title: Related articles
criteria.description: Suggested posts relevant to the current post

criteria.title: Opt-in for subscription
criteria.description: A signup form for users to join which will subscribe them to a platform that lets you notify them of new posts

criteria.title: Date posted
criteria.description: When the post was shared live

criteria.title: Tags
criteria.description: A specific category for users to explore as a topic

criteria.title: Comments
criteria.description: A section for discussion that users can join and contribute to

checklists.name: Contact Us
checklists.description: A contact us page provides visitors with methods to communicate with an organization. It typically includes a contact form, business address, phone numbers, email addresses, and sometimes a location.

criteria.title: Personality and branding
criteria.description: Visual character and tone of voice that align with your brand
criteria.suggestion: Colloquial copy helps you appears more accessible to users

criteria.title: Clear methods to contact
criteria.description: Phone number, email or a form to fill in for examples

criteria.title: Social media accounts
criteria.description: User may feel more comfortable contacting via a social platform

criteria.title: Segmenting contact methods
criteria.description: If you have different contacts for support and sales, showcase that! It shows you have specific support for their issue

criteria.title: Easy location to get to
criteria.description: Make this page available in your header or footer

checklists.name: Pricing
checklists.description: A pricing page presents product or service costs, features, and plan comparisons in a clear, organized format. It helps users understand different pricing tiers, included features, and subscription options, enabling them to make informed purchasing decisions.

criteria.title: Pricing options
criteria.description: Subscriptions plans or one-off purchase

criteria.title: Pricing features
criteria.description: What the user will get for purchasing the product

criteria.title: A free pathway to sign up
criteria.description: A way for user to try your product before considering purchase
criteria.suggestion: Clearly state the length of the trial period before being charged

criteria.title: Refund or return policy
criteria.description: A user may want to understand this further

criteria.title: Highlighted price as a recommendation
criteria.description: Showcase a price that most users purchase, or they will get the best value from

criteria.title: Security logo for payment processing
criteria.description: Show how you process purchases with a credible vendor for legibility

criteria.title: Frequency of payments (monthly vs yearly)
criteria.description: You may offer an annual option for long term customers that are rewarded with a discount

checklists.name: FAQ
checklists.description: A FAQ (frequently asked questions) page provides answers to common user queries in a structured, easy-to-scan format. It serves as a self-service resource to address typical customer concerns, reduce support inquiries, and help users find solutions quickly.

criteria.title: Purposeful information
criteria.description: Ensure the questions and answers shown are providing value to the users to make decisions about your product

criteria.title: Contact options
criteria.description: If a user doesn't have their problem solved or question answered, offer a method for them to directly contact you
criteria.suggestion: Order your contact options by accessibility - your first option should be the easiest for the user, following in an ascending order of level of effort

criteria.title: Table of contents
criteria.description: If you have a large amount of questions, structure your topics so users can navigate between areas easier

criteria.title: Search functionality
criteria.description: Keyword search for users to look up their questions

criteria.title: Navigate by topic
criteria.description: Segment your questions into general topics to structure your content and enable an easier search for users

checklists.description: A 404 page appears when users attempt to access a non-existent or moved webpage. It communicates the error in a friendly way and helps users navigate back to working pages through suggested links, search functionality, or a return to homepage option.

criteria.title: Logo
criteria.description: Either your complete logo or a symbol mark

criteria.title: Title
criteria.description: Make it clear the user is on the 404 page

criteria.title: Description
criteria.description: Explain why the user has landed on this page

criteria.title: Links to other pages
criteria.description: Offer pathways to stick around
criteria.suggestion: Include a link to visit the homepage Include a link that allows user to contact Include a search bar to allow user to look for something

criteria.title: Illustrations, patterns, visual flair
criteria.description: This page is a great opportunity to show off your brand's personality

checklists.name: Login
checklists.description: A login page is a critical component of many web applications and websites, serving as the gateway for users to access personalized features, secure content, and their own data.

criteria.title: Logo
criteria.description: Either your complete logo or a symbol mark

criteria.title: Title
criteria.description: Tell the user this is where they login

criteria.title: Account identification
criteria.description: A unique identifier for the user
criteria.suggestion: Consider multiple identifiers to login with e.g. username, or email address, or phone number

criteria.title: Password
criteria.description: A secure, private code that allows access to their account
criteria.suggestion: Create the ability to make the password visible

criteria.title: Link to reset password
criteria.description: A user may forget their unique code - let them change it!
criteria.suggestion: Position this link close to your password input field

criteria.title: Link to sign up
criteria.description: A user may not have an account and landed on this page anyway

criteria.title: Login via third party
criteria.description: Turn text fields into one click by allowing users to connect via a third party e.g. Google, Apple, Facebook, Twitter

criteria.title: Testimonial
criteria.description: Reinforcing the brand and product never goes out of style

criteria.title: Blog post
criteria.description: An opportunity to show off content relevant to the user

criteria.title: New feature
criteria.description: The perfect way to build excitement for something new right before a user is about to log in and see it!

checklists.name: Blog
checklists.description: A blog page aggregates and displays multiple articles or posts in a chronological order, typically showing previews, titles, publication dates, and categories. It provides easy navigation through pagination or infinite scroll, allowing users to browse and discover content.

criteria.title: Hero
criteria.description: A clear indicator it's a blog, whether it's for an individual, team or company

criteria.title: Navigation
criteria.description: A logo, links to visit, a CTA, and potentially a search function
criteria.suggestion: Utilise navigational links to show sub topics

criteria.title: Layout
criteria.description: How sections and blog posts are structured
criteria.suggestion: Consider what's above the fold on mobile, tablet and desktop Consider blog article order (newest first, trending) A grid layout with multiple posts on a row has more density

criteria.title: Blog post preview
criteria.description: The visuals and text of a blog post
criteria.suggestion: Typography hierarchy is important here - a user must clearly see the heading first A branded thumbnail sets the mood of the content If you include a description, it should be economical in clearly explaining the blog post

criteria.title: Description
criteria.description: Summarise what's covered in the blog — shown in the hero

criteria.title: Tags and/or categories
criteria.description: A topic that can be attached to a blog post for convenient filtering

criteria.title: Search function
criteria.description: Have lots of posts? Search makes it easier for the user to find the content they desire

criteria.title: Opt-in for subscription
criteria.description: A signup form for users to complete to make them a subscriber of the blog's content

criteria.title: Sidebar
criteria.description: This can contain additional links and resources that support the blog posts e.g. search function, popular posts, trending topics

criteria.title: Pagination
criteria.description: Break up your content into pages after 10-20 items (there are pros and cons on both sides of the pagination vs infinite scroll argument, so go with what suits your product better!)

checklists.name: Sign up
checklists.description: A sign up page enables new users to create an account by providing required information through a form. It guides users through the registration process, validates input data, and establishes their credentials for accessing restricted features or personalized content.

criteria.title: Logo
criteria.description: Either your complete logo or a symbol mark

criteria.title: Title
criteria.description: Tell the user this is where they create an account

criteria.title: Description
criteria.description: Describe the basic features of creating an account and set their expectations as to what they can achieve

criteria.title: Account identification
criteria.description: A unique identifier for the user to log in with
criteria.suggestion: An email address is the most commonly used, as you are also gaining a method to communicate with them beyond whatever they do next

criteria.title: Setting a password
criteria.description: A secure, private code that allows them to access their account in the future
criteria.suggestion: Include a password strength indicator Include password requirements (length, special characters) Create the ability to make the password visible

criteria.title: Link to login
criteria.description: A user may already have an account and landed on this page anyway

criteria.title: Sign up via third party
criteria.description: Reduce a few clicks to one, by allowing users to sign up via Facebook or Google

criteria.title: Current active customer count
criteria.description: Showcasing how many people are using and enjoying your product can evoke a fear of missing out for potential users

criteria.title: Testimonial or social proof
criteria.description: Reinforcing the brand and product never goes out of style

criteria.title: Blog post
criteria.description: An opportunity to show off some amazing content to convert an unsure lead

criteria.title: Billing plans and trial period (if payment is involved)
criteria.description: Clearly define the length of the trial period and when they will be charged
